MUQATIL:23:101-105/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r1.claim: The trumpet blast is the second one; family relations such as uncle, cousin, brother, and nephew will not avail, and close friends will not ask after each other.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r4.claim: The trumpet is a horn, a point Yaḥyā says was explained earlier.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r5.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r5.claim: The Prophet says no one asks another at three points: while scales are set, while records fly, and at the bridge, until each learns his fate.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says family ties remain recognizable, as in the day a person flees relatives; people see one another in some scenes but do not recognize one another in others.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r7.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says lineage no longer produces mutual affection or requests for kin to bear another's burden as it did in worldly life.

TAB-FULL:v17p112/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse refers to the first trumpet blast, when no earthly thing remains; the exchange in 37:27 happens after they enter Paradise.

TAB-FULL:v17p112/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r2.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the blast as the first one.

TAB-FULL:v17p112/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the first blast leaves no living creature except God, while questioning one another occurs after resurrection at the second blast.

TAB-FULL:v17p112/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r4.claim: On the first-blast interpretation, those overcome by the blast cannot communicate through kinship, ask about one another's state or lineage, or visit one another.

TAB-FULL:v17p112/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r5.claim: Other interpreters say the verse refers instead to the second blast.

TAB-FULL:v17p112/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v17p112/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd describes a public call for anyone owed a right by a person, including relatives, explaining why kinship cannot protect them from claims.

TAB-FULL:v17p113/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says claims are settled by transferring the debtor's good deeds to claimants; if they run out, claimants' sins are added, and the debtor is sent to Hell.

TAB-FULL:v17p113/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r2.speaker: حجاج
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r2.claim: No one can appeal to lineage, ask for anything, or claim kinship ties on that day.

TAB-FULL:v17p113/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r3.claim: Qatada says people dread seeing acquaintances on Judgment Day because they fear being asked to settle a claim, citing the verse about each person being occupied by his own affair.

TAB-FULL:v17p113/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v17p113/r4.claim: The Prophet says a caller from the Throne will tell people who wronged one another to settle their claims and then enter Paradise.

ZAJJAJ:v4p21#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p21#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p21#2/r4.claim: The verse may refer to the first blast or after the second; ṣūr is a horn, while the lexicographers' claim that it means forms is weak.

ZAJJAJ:v4p21#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p21#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p21#2/r5.claim: No mutual questioning does not conflict with other verses: Judgment has changing stages; questions may seek information or rebuke, and day can mean a span of time.

NAHHAS:v3p121/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p121/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v3p121/r7.claim: One explanation is that people will be at a time when they do not ask one another; yawm can mean a known period.

NAHHAS:v3p121/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p121/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p121/r8.claim: The clearer sense is that family lineage will no longer be a source of boasting or questioning as it was in worldly life.

SULAMI:v2p39#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p39#2/r1.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v2p39#2/r1.claim: Lineage means seeing one's own deeds and hoping for sincerity through them; people do not ask one another because they are absorbed in their condition rather than worldly comfort or misery.

THALABI:v7p56/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p56/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
THALABI:v7p56/r1.claim: He compares the statement about no lineage to the verse saying no close friend asks about another.

THALABI:v7p56/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p56/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
THALABI:v7p56/r2.claim: He says no one can ask for anything by invoking kinship, and people do not ask one another through family ties.

THALABI:v7p56/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p56/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p56/r3.claim: He identifies the trumpet blast here as the first blast, when creation faints; after the next blast people rise and question one another.

THALABI:v7p56/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p56/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v7p56/r4.claim: He identifies the trumpet blast here as the second blast.

THALABI:v7p57/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v7p57/r1.claim: His report says God settles claims by taking from a sinner's good deeds; a faithful person with surplus good deeds has them multiplied, citing the promise that God does not wrong even an atom.

THALABI:v7p57/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v7p57/r2.claim: If the sinner's good deeds run out while claimants remain, their bad deeds are added to his and he is assigned a place in the Fire.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r1.claim: They may not recognize one another because terror overwhelms them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r2.claim: Though they recognize kin, they do not maintain or meet through those bonds, as each flees even a brother.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r3.claim: They do not ask kin to carry another's burden or help one another.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r4.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p67/r4.claim: They do not ask for news because each is occupied with himself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, identifies this as the first trumpet blast, which makes creation swoon except those God wills to spare.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r10.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r10.claim: Abu Ali says إذا cannot be governed by نفخ or by the clause after لا, since what follows لا cannot govern what precedes it; an omitted verb governs it instead.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r11.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r11.claim: The omitted verb can be understood as lineages being severed or becoming useless when the trumpet is blown; the syntax is discussed at 34:7.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r2.claim: At that moment people cannot recognize one another, ask about one another, or show kin-based affection because each is absorbed in himself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r3.claim: In Ata's reading of the scene, the trumpet is the second blast; lineage no longer serves for boasting or the worldly question about one's tribe.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masud and Muqatil also identify the trumpet blast here as the second one.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says family members will be more attached to one another than in worldly life, and he recited this verse as evidence.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r6.claim: The verse requires an understood qualification: lineages remain, but contact, mutual affection, boasting, and inquiry through lineage cease.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r7.claim: This does not conflict with 37:27: the Resurrection has different phases, some so overwhelming that people cannot ask, and others when they recover and ask.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, when asked about the two passages, says these are successive phases of the Resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p66#2/r9.claim: In a report through Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas places the mutual questioning in Paradise after people enter it.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:96-101/r7.claim: At the final trumpet blast, people will not boast about lineage or ask about one another's tribe and ancestry as they did in worldly life.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r1.claim: The trumpet is a horn blown by Israfil announcing the resurrection, according to most exegetes; Hasan instead says it is the breathing of spirit into images.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says this is the first blast, while Ibn Masud says it is the second.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r3.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r3.claim: No relations means people do not maintain ties or show affection through kinship.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that people will not boast about lineage as they did in worldly life.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r5.claim: A further interpretation is that they will not seek rescue by calling on their clans as people do in this world.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r6.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r6.claim: Abu Ali interprets 'they do not ask one another' as not asking after each other's state.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r7.claim: Another explanation is that they cannot ask one another to bear their sins.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r1.claim: He identifies this as the first blast; they fall unconscious, then rise after the next blast and converse.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r2.claim: He identifies it as the second blast; people are summoned to settle rights even against relatives, so lineage offers no protection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r3.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission it is the second blast; people do not boast of lineage or ask social introductions, though kinship itself remains.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r4.claim: The report that every bond and lineage ends except the Prophet’s is explained as faith and Qur’an being his surviving bond and lineage.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429/r5.claim: The apparent contrast with people conversing elsewhere is resolved by different stages: terror silences them in one place; they recover and converse in another.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r1.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r1.claim: Al-Hasan reads ṣūr with fatḥa on the waw.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r2.claim: Abu Razin is reported to read ṣūr with either kasra or fatḥa, supporting the interpretation that it means a collection of forms.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r3.claim: The denial of kinship may mean people are separated into punishment and reward, with deeds replacing family ties; kinship also fails to prompt compassion as each flees relatives.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads “they will not ask one another,” assimilating ta into sin.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206/r5.claim: Apparent contradictions with 70:10, 37:27, 52:25 and 10:45 have two solutions: different periods and states during the fifty-thousand-year Day, or nonrecognition at the first blast followed by recognition and questions after the second.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p155#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and others place the loss of kinship at the first trumpet, when everyone dies; Ibn Atiyya objects that this removes the verse's reference to the terror of gathering.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r1.claim: Ibn Masud and others say kinship no longer helps after the second trumpet because people are overwhelmed and each is occupied with himself; Ibn Atiyya calls this interpretation good.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r2.claim: Qatada says a person will fear anyone he recognizes because of a possible unpaid grievance; people flee relatives, and everyone is glad to have a claim against family.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r3.claim: Questioning and recognition are also absent during this overwhelming stage, although later scenes of resurrection include questions and recognition.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r1.claim: An implied verb is needed for the interpretation that people will neither boast by lineage nor show kinship based compassion.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:23:101-108/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Jubbāʾī say the verse denies boasting about lineage; people will be distinguished by deeds, not ancestry.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r3.claim: Either interpretation requires an understood verb: they will not boast by lineage or show kinship-based compassion, and no one will outrank another by ancestry.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:23:101-108/r4.claim: A prophetic report says every lineage and noble descent is severed on Judgment Day except the Prophet’s own lineage and kinship.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r5.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:23:101-108/r5.claim: They do not ask about one another’s condition as they did in worldly life, since each is preoccupied with himself.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:23:101-108/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that they do not ask others to carry their sins for them.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:23:101-108/r7.claim: There is no conflict with people questioning one another elsewhere: the Resurrection has different stages, some so terrifying that no one asks, and others when they do.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r8.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:23:101-108/r8.claim: A further view places the questioning among the people of Paradise as they enter it, after they are safe from the terrors of Judgment.

TABRISI:23:101/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101/r7.claim: In the clause beginning idhā nufikha, the governing element is the phrase baynahum; yawmaʾidhin is the predicate of an elided lā, understood as no kinship remains among them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the trumpet blast as the first.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r2.claim: Another view identifies it as the second blast.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r3.claim: The wording leaves an ellipsis: no kinships by which people boast or sever ties; family lines themselves do not disappear, but social contact and boasting do.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r4.claim: One interpretation of not asking one another is that no one claims kinship so another will surrender his due.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that they do not ask about one another's condition because each is preoccupied with himself.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r6.claim: A third interpretation is that Arabs will not ask which tribe someone belongs to in order to assess his standing.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p490#2/r7.claim: He refers the continuation through the statement that fire scorches faces to his earlier explanation at 7:8.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r1.claim: Kinship itself remains because the resurrected are the same children and parents; what is denied is the practical effect of kinship.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r10.claim: They are occupied with themselves after the first blast; after the next blast they turn to each other and ask who raised them from their resting place.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r11.claim: “They do not ask” can mean that they do not ask about kinship claims.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r12.claim: Another reconciliation takes the statement as describing disbelievers, whose fear is especially severe.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r2.claim: Kinship normally brings compassion and mutual appeal, but terror occupies each person with himself and prevents attention to relatives.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r3.claim: Kinship can invite boasting and questions about lineage, but people have no leisure for that in the afterlife.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r4.claim: The denial can also be a metaphor for extreme fear, when everyone is distracted even from children, siblings, and close kin.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reports that a caller will summon anyone with a claim against a named person; then a woman will rejoice to have a right against even close family.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r6.claim: Qatada says a person will dread seeing anyone familiar on Judgment Day, fearing that the acquaintance may claim a right against him.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r7.claim: In answer to Aisha, the Prophet says people are distracted from recognition at three scenes: receiving the record, the scales, and the Bridge over Hell.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r8.speaker: الملاحدة
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r8.claim: Some object that the denial of questioning and recognition conflicts with verses where people question one another and recognize one another.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106#2/r9.claim: The fifty-thousand-year Day contains different states: people recognize and question one another at some times and are bewildered at others.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r1.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r1.claim: The first and preferred explanation takes the Trumpet as a horn in which a mighty sound is blown, marking the world's destruction and the resurrection; the Prophet calls it a horn.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r2.claim: Hasan understands the Trumpet as all forms collectively, with their spirits blown into them; he reads the word with a fatḥa on the wāw.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r3.speaker: أبو رزين
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r3.claim: Abu Razin's fatḥa and kasra readings support interpreting the word as the plural of form.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r4.claim: A third view treats blowing the Trumpet as a metaphor for resurrection and gathering.

RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p106/r5.claim: Al-Razi prefers the literal horn because of the prophetic report; the second blowing also shows that the phrase cannot simply mean the nonrepeating act of enlivening a spirit.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r1.claim: The reciprocal questioning described just before belongs to the people of Paradise after they enter it.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101#2/r1.claim: The report continues that a person devoted to God who has even a mustard seed of good deeds has them multiplied and enters Paradise, citing the verse that God does not wrong an atom’s weight.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101#2/r2.claim: If the person is wretched and has no good deeds left while creditors remain, the angels transfer their misdeeds to him and issue his writ to Hell.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r1.claim: The trumpet here is the second blowing.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says people will neither boast of family descent nor ask one another about tribe and lineage, and they will not recognize one another because terror overwhelms them.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r3.claim: An alternative places this at the first blowing, when all creatures swoon; at the second they rise and ask one another. Explaining the apparent conflict with 37:50, Ibn Abbas says no living person remains after the first, while questioning occurs after entering Paradise.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says this verse concerns the second blowing.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r5.speaker: أبو عمر زاذان
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r5.claim: Abu Umar Zadhan recounts that when he complained to Ibn Masud that his foreign origin kept him from access, Ibn Masud drew him close and described the Day of Judgment, when a caller summons people owed rights; a woman rejoices at a claim against relatives.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:23:101/r6.claim: In the same report, God orders people’s rights restored; since worldly wealth is gone, good deeds are distributed to claimants, and the verse denies the usefulness of family ties then.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r1.claim: The trumpet is blown for the Hour; a reading with an open wāw supports interpreting ṣūr as a plural of image.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r2.claim: Kinship is useless because terror removes tenderness and compassion and people flee relatives; alternatively, lineage may be useless for boasting.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r3.claim: They do not question one another because each is occupied with himself; this does not conflict with later mutual questioning, which occurs after accounting or after entry into Paradise and Hell.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r1.claim: One view identifies the trumpet blast as the second blast.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r2.claim: The Abū ʿAmr reading assimilates the two identical consonants across the word boundary; family ties will not connect people then, and only deeds will.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131/r3.claim: There is no contradiction with the verse where people turn to one another asking questions: fear silences them at one stage, then they recover and ask at another.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says kinship disappears at the first trumpet because people die then; this interpretation lessens the horror of the gathering.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and others place the severing of kinship when people rise from graves: each is preoccupied, ending reliance on and boasting through family ties.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r3.claim: Qatāda says a person most dislikes meeting someone he knows that day, for fear of an unpaid grievance; the passage echoes the flight from relatives in 80:34–36.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r4.claim: Another explanation is that family members do not connect when separated for their allotted reward or punishment; only deeds create their connection.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r5.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads “wa-lā yasāʾalūn” with a doubled sīn, assimilating the tāʾ of the underlying “yataṣāʾalūn.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r6.claim: The absence of questions here does not conflict with questions in 37:27 because resurrection has different stages; questions may occur at the second trumpet after their absence at the first.

SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r1.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on ṣād and a still wāw in الصور.

SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read with fatḥa on wāw, making it the plural of صورة.

SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r3.speaker: أبو رزين
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r3.claim: Abu Razin has the anomalous reading with kasra on ṣād and fatḥa on wāw, inverted from the pattern لحى.

SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r4.claim: أنساب means blood kinship and can figuratively mean social connection; it is originally a verbal noun.

SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r5.speaker: شاعر مجهول
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r5.claim: A poem says there is no lineage or friendship today, using نسب for kinship and خلة for intimacy.

SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:101/r6.claim: بينهم and يومئذ may attach directly to أنساب; alternatively بينهم describes أنساب, while يومئذ's tanwin replaces the omitted clause يوم إذ ينفخ في الصور.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r1.claim: At the resurrection blast, kinship will not help: a parent will not pity or defend a child, even when the relative was once dearest.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r2.claim: God will call those with claims against others to collect them; people will welcome a claim even against a parent, child, or spouse, however small.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r3.speaker: المسور بن مخرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r3.claim: The Prophet says Fāṭima is part of him and that his kinship ties will endure at the Resurrection while other lineages end; Ibn Kathīr notes a related sound report in both Ṣaḥīḥs.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p495/r4.claim: The Prophet says his kinship remains joined in this life and the next and he will precede people at the watering place; he knows their ancestry, but says they changed religion after him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r1.claim: ʿUmar says he married Umm Kulthūm, daughter of ʿAlī, because he heard that every bond and lineage ends at the Resurrection except the Prophet's.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r2.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says every lineage and marriage bond ends on the Last Day except the Prophet's lineage and affinity.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496/r3.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says the Prophet asked that anyone he married into or who married into his community be with him in Paradise, and God granted it.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r1.claim: The trumpet is either the second blast of resurrection or the third blast for fainting; people then rise from graves or from their fainting.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r2.claim: Kinship will no longer be invoked for boasting or mutual aid amid terror and distraction; only righteous deeds matter, and no one can help another without God's permission.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r3.claim: The denial of questioning here concerns mutual support, while questioning elsewhere concerns blame and quarrels at different long stages of the Day, so the reports do not conflict.

DURR-FULL:v6p116/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says that at the first trumpet blast no living being remains except God.

DURR-FULL:v6p116/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r4.claim: Al-Suddi places the absence of kinship and questioning at the first trumpet blast.

DURR-FULL:v6p116/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r5.claim: Qatada says no one asks another about ancestry or kinship then; Ibn Jurayj likewise says no one appeals by lineage or kinship.

DURR-FULL:v6p116/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reconciles these verses by placing the absence of kinship at the first blast and mutual questioning after the later blast, or after entry to Paradise.

DURR-FULL:v6p116/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p116/r7.claim: On Judgment Day, a caller names each person, and anyone with a claim may demand justice even from a parent, child, or spouse; people may be glad to hold a claim against kin.

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r1.claim: The verse is cited as scriptural confirmation that kinship will not prevent claims on Judgment Day.

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r2.claim: Qatada says a person most fears seeing an acquaintance on Judgment Day lest that person demand something, then cites the fleeing from one’s brother.

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r3.speaker: المسور بن مخرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r3.claim: The Prophet says all lineages end on Judgment Day except his own lineage, bond, and in-law connection.

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r4.claim: The Prophet says every bond and lineage is severed on Judgment Day except his bond and lineage.

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r5.claim: The Prophet says every lineage and marriage connection is severed except his lineage and in-law relationship.

BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r2.claim: The trumpet blast is the second one that raises the dead; the horn-like trumpet is a means God uses to return souls to their bodies.

BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r3.claim: Kinship will not benefit them, either because panic erases tenderness and makes relatives flee one another or because there will be no lineage to boast about; lineage is shared parentage, vertically or among collateral relatives.

BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r4.claim: People will not ask one another's identity or tribe because each is absorbed in himself by terror and cannot recognize others.

BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r5.claim: This does not contradict people later questioning one another: the lack of questions is at the onset of the second blast before reckoning, or during stations when terror overwhelms them; later they recover and converse.

BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r6.claim: In a report from Aisha, the Prophet says there are three places where everyone is distracted: when books are delivered, at the scales, and on the bridge over Hell.

BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v6p75#3/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says each servant will be publicly named and creditors invited to claim their due; people will rejoice if a right is established against even a close relative.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r1.claim: The trumpet is blown for Resurrection in the second blast, when resurrection and gathering occur.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r2.claim: Alternatively ṣūr means plural ṣūrah, image: souls are blown into bodies. Readings from Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Ibn ʿIyāḍ, and Ibn Razīn support this; it can coincide with blowing the horn.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r3.claim: Kinship will not benefit people: terror and absorption in each person’s fate make family ties effectively nonexistent, as the cited flight from relatives illustrates.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v18p64#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports a public call on Judgment Day inviting anyone owed a right or grievance to claim it, even when the debtor is family; this supports a general reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r1.claim: Reports from Maswar ibn Makhrama and Ibn ʿUmar preserve the Prophetic exception that every bond and lineage is severed except his; al-Ālūsī accepts it but limits benefit to related believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r2.claim: The lineage report does not limit the verse: just after the second blast people do not notice or think of kinship, describing terror rather than denying benefit to believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Jubbāʾī say people will not boast of lineage but pride themselves on deeds and escape from terrors; on this reading negation is figurative.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r4.claim: Adding ‘beneficial,’ ‘noticed,’ or ‘boasted of’ to ‘lineages’ is possible but weak; the time adverb attaches to ‘among them,’ not ‘lineages.’

ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r5.claim: They do not ask about identity or condition because each is absorbed in himself; silence begins just after the second blast, before or after recognition.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p65/r6.claim: Later mutual questioning may occur near Hell for unbelievers and in Paradise for believers; the negation may mean recognition or requests for benefit, unlike later blame or companionship.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66/r1.claim: One Ibn ʿAbbās report puts absent questioning at the first blast and its return at the second; his other report takes this verse’s blast as the second and allows other reconciliations.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads the verb with a doubled sīn, yusāʾalūn, ‘they are questioned.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r2.claim: The trumpet clause branches from the resurrection deadline: instead of saying when resurrection comes, it paints the scene of the trumpet being blown.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r3.claim: The ṣūr is a horn blown for assembly or alarm, used for war and Jewish prayer; a Bukhārī report on the beginning of the call to prayer is cited, as is 6:73.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r4.claim: The passive verb emphasizes the occurrence of the blowing rather than who blows; God commands it, or an angel such as Isrāfīl does so.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.claim: The main consequence concerns the weighed deeds, answering the rejected plea for return; the denial of kinship first cuts off hope of help or intercession.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r6.claim: The most likely answer to when the trumpet is blown is the later question about how long they stayed on earth; intervening material is parenthetical.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r1.claim: The pronoun in baynahum refers to the preceding plural pronouns, namely the polytheists.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r2.claim: Denying kinship denies its customary benefits of support, rescue, and intercession, indirectly saying there is no helper.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r3.claim: Questioning one another means asking for help during the terror, as in 70:10; the questioning in 37:27–33 occurs after they despair of any helper or intercessor.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r4.claim: In Bukhārī, Ibn ʿAbbās answers Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq that the denial of kinship and questioning is at the first trumpet, while mutual questioning is after the second.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#5/r7.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:23:99-118#5/r7.claim: A report says every lineage and kinship is cut off on Judgment Day except the Prophet's lineage and family connection.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r1.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r1.claim: Other reports preserve the exception with varying wording: the Prophet's lineage, relation, and in-law ties remain.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r2.speaker: زين العابدين
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r2.claim: Al-Sajjad says Paradise is for obedient people regardless of ancestry and Fire for disobedient people regardless of Qurayshi descent; only righteous deeds sent ahead will help.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r3.claim: The verse's context resists limiting its general denial of kinship; a possible benefit of the Prophet's lineage is that his descendants are enabled to do good deeds that help them.

TABATABAI:23:99-118/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:23:99-118/r4.claim: The trumpet is the second blast that revives the dead, not the first blast that kills the living, because the listed consequences belong to the resurrection.

TABATABAI:23:99-118/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118/r5.claim: The denial of family ties negates their worldly effects: kinship matters for household and social cooperation, which has no place in the accounting and recompense of Resurrection.

TABATABAI:23:99-118/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118/r6.claim: “Nor ask one another” names the clearest effect of kinship, asking relatives about each other to seek help and avert harm; this concerns the reckoning, not later inhabitants of Paradise or Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p282/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p282/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p282/r5.claim: At the trumpet, family and tribal bonds will not help, and people will have no time even to seek help from one another; such aid was especially important among Arabs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p282/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p282/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p282/r6.claim: Here tasaʾul means seeking mutual help from one another.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:99/r6.claim: Family ties will not help in the afterlife, demonstrating absolute justice; people’s inability to question one another conveys the terror of the reckoning.

STUDYQURAN:23:101/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:101/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:101/r1.claim: The trumpet announces the world's end and the approaching Judgment.

STUDYQURAN:23:101/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:101/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:101/r2.claim: The severing of worldly bonds is illustrated elsewhere by a nursing woman forgetting her child and a man fleeing his brother.

STUDYQURAN:23:101/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:101/r3.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:23:101/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī reconciles verses that deny and affirm questioning by treating Judgment as a long sequence of states: terror prevents concern for others at some times, while other states allow it.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
